description: Köppen climate classification system and Earth's major climate zones

koppen_classification.overview: Most widely used climate classification system, developed by Wladimir Köppen (1884)

A_tropical.definition: All months average ≥18°C; no cold season

subtypes.Af: Tropical rainforest; rain all year; Amazon, Congo basin
subtypes.Aw: Tropical savanna; dry winter; sub-Saharan Africa, Brazil

C_temperate.definition: Warmest month >10°C; coldest month between -3°C and 18°C

subtypes.Cfa: Humid subtropical; SE USA, E China, SE Brazil
subtypes.Cfb: Oceanic; NW Europe, Pacific NW USA, S Chile
subtypes.Csa: Mediterranean; hot dry summer; Mediterranean Basin, California

D_continental.definition: Warmest month >10°C; coldest month <-3°C; large temperature range

subtypes.Dfa: Hot summer continental; US Midwest, N China
subtypes.Dfb: Warm summer continental; E Europe, Great Lakes

subtypes.ET: Tundra; warmest month 0–10°C; Arctic coast, high mountains
subtypes.EF: Ice cap; warmest month <0°C; Antarctica, Greenland interior

climate_drivers.latitude: Determines solar angle; tropics warmest, poles coldest
climate_drivers.ocean_currents: Warm currents (Gulf Stream) moderate coastal temperatures; cold currents cool
climate_drivers.continentality: Interior landmasses have more extreme temperatures than coastal areas
climate_drivers.prevailing_winds: Determine moisture; trade winds, westerlies, polar easterlies
climate_drivers.orographic_effect: Mountains force air up (rain), then descend dry (rain shadow)

mediterranean.characteristics: Hot dry summer, mild wet winter

monsoon.definition: Seasonal wind reversal causing wet and dry seasons
monsoon.summer_monsoon: Moist ocean air brings heavy rain (South/Southeast Asia, June–September)

maritime.characteristics: Mild temperatures year-round, frequent cloud and rain
maritime.cause: Proximity to ocean buffers temperature extremes

climate_change_impacts.temperature: Global average surface temperature increased ~1.1°C since pre-industrial (2023)
climate_change_impacts.precipitation: Wet areas getting wetter; dry areas drier
climate_change_impacts.extreme_events: More frequent heatwaves, intense hurricanes, heavy rainfall events
climate_change_impacts.arctic: Warming 3× faster than global average; sea ice decline
